text:
This project is pre-indexed by Scalpel. Follow this workflow:
1. Call build_context with the task description to get a relevance-ranked, budgeted project context; use get_project_map for a structural overview (raise budget_tokens if it reports truncated=true).
2. To understand a requirement, call search_documents: it matches term by term and already returns the FULL text of its best matches, so read them instead of re-reading those paragraphs. Only if it returns nothing useful, change the terms (a synonym, the identifier) rather than rephrasing the same one. Every block is addressed by PATH: file.md::Section mere::Paragraphe, file.cs::Classe::Methode, or a directory path. read_block(path) answers what that path names -- a directory lists its complete contents, a file lists its complete outline, a paragraph or a symbol returns its WHOLE numbered text -- and none of those lists is ever truncated or paged. read_block(paths=[...]) reads several blocks in ONE call.
   Document sections expose referenced_files: if a requirement names a file to update, locate that EXACT workspace file (search_documents with no query lists every document) and edit it; never edit an unrelated document.
3. To read or change code, call search_symbols with view='contract' to see the signature and callers of every match IN THAT CALL, then view='implementation' on the one you will change: the implementation view carries the 1-based numbers AND the content_hash edit_block expects, so you can edit straight from it, with no read_block in between.
4. To CHANGE existing code or documentation, call edit_block(path, expected_hash, ops=[...]) on the 1-based numbers you already hold. Call read_block first ONLY when you have no recent read of that block (or after an edit is refused as stale). Operations: {"replace": [first, last], "content": ...}, {"delete": [first, last]}, or {"insert_after": n, "content": ...}. replace takes a RANGE [first, last]: replace a whole sub-block in ONE operation rather than one operation per line. Send ONLY the new content, at the indentation you see (the numbered lines show the real one): your lines are inserted literally, the tool only keeps the block's base aligned to its AST level, and it returns the updated numbered block and its new hash, so you never need to re-read after an edit. BATCH YOUR CHANGES: every assistant message costs a full turn. When you have several changes that do not depend on each other (different blocks, different files), send them ALL in the SAME message -- several tool calls in one message, or one edit_block(edits=[{path, expected_hash, ops}, ...]). Only a second change to the SAME block must wait for the hash the first one returns. There is no whole-block rewrite: a full rewrite is a replace over lines 1..line_count. To ADD a block call insert_block(parent=..., text=...): the PARENT nature decides the syntax -- under a code file (or under a symbol) the text is code, under a document it is a Markdown paragraph whose first line is the title, under a directory its first line is the name of the file or directory to create. To remove a block call delete_block(path). The AST tools OWN indentation: never edit a block just to change it.
Budget: at most 4 searches per concept. If a search already returned the text, act on it; do not keep rephrasing the same query.
